SUMMARY: Real-time equity trade blotter — core scope (view/create/amend/cancel, live push, persisted, tested)
USER_STORY: As a trader/ops user, I want a live trade blotter where I can view, create, amend, and cancel trades and see every change pushed to all connected clients instantly, so that I always work from a single up-to-date view without manual refreshing.
DESCRIPTION: Covers the brief's full required scope end to end: Express + Prisma/Postgres backend (real CRUD, no mocks), a raw `ws` WebSocket broadcaster wired into every mutation, and a React/TanStack frontend that renders, filters, sorts, and reconciles real-time events into its query cache. All 20 sub-tasks below are Done — verified via `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, the full 39-test suite (shared 16, backend 12 incl. live-Postgres integration tests, frontend 11 incl. a mocked-WebSocket cache-reconciliation test), and a manual end-to-end `docker compose up` + curl walkthrough of create->amend->cancel->409->404. See ARCH.md §13 — this project intentionally combines Day-0 and Day-1 into one pass, so nothing here is mock data awaiting a later real-wiring task.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: All of: (1) GET/POST/PATCH/POST-cancel endpoints live against real Postgres; (2) every mutation broadcasts a typed WS event received by all connected clients; (3) frontend grid reflects real-time events without a page refresh; (4) pnpm test/pnpm lint/pnpm typecheck all pass; (5) docker compose up boots postgres+backend+frontend healthily from a clean state.

SUMMARY: Shared Trade domain type & WebSocket event envelope types
USER_STORY: As a developer on either the frontend or backend, I want one shared Trade type and WS event envelope, so that client and server never drift on trade shape or event contracts.
DESCRIPTION: Implements shared/src/trade.ts (the Trade domain type extending the brief's minimum shape with book/counterparty per ARCH §4) and shared/src/events.ts (the TRADE_CREATED/TRADE_AMENDED/TRADE_CANCELLED envelope types per ARCH §6). Consumed directly by both backend/src/repositories/tradeRepository.ts and frontend/src/lib/apiClient.ts — read and confirmed no duplicate type definitions exist on either side. **Day 1:** no swap needed — these are permanent shared type definitions, not mock data; both backend and frontend already import them directly.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Trade type includes book and counterparty; TradeEvent union covers all 3 mutation types with a payload: Trade; both types imported (not redefined) in backend and frontend.

SUMMARY: Shared Zod validation schemas (create/amend/list-query)
USER_STORY: As a developer, I want one Zod schema per trade operation shared from shared/, so that client-side form validation and server-side request validation can never disagree.
DESCRIPTION: Implements shared/src/schemas.ts — createTradeSchema, amendTradeSchema (a .partial() of create), and tradeListQuerySchema. Imported directly by backend/src/routes/trades.ts (.parse() at the API boundary) and by frontend/src/components/CreateTradeModal.tsx/AmendTradeModal.tsx (zodResolver). Has its own dedicated unit test suite (shared/src/schemas.test.ts, part of the 16 passing shared tests) per ARCH §12's explicit call to test schemas directly rather than only through their callers. **Day 1:** no swap needed — this is the single real validation source of truth already wired into both the API boundary and the forms, not a placeholder.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: createTradeSchema rejects non-positive quantity/price and empty strings; amendTradeSchema accepts partial payloads; tradeListQuerySchema validates all 6 documented query params; schema unit tests pass.

SUMMARY: Prisma schema, migrations & DB-level check constraints
USER_STORY: As a backend developer, I want the trades table and its migrations defined in database/, so that the schema is versioned and DB-level integrity rules back up app-level validation.
DESCRIPTION: Implements database/schema.prisma (Trade model + Side/TradeStatus enums, indexes on symbol/trader/status/tradeTimestamp per ARCH §4) and two migrations: 20260922142840_init and 20260922142859_add_check_constraints (adds CHECK (quantity > 0) / CHECK (price > 0), since Prisma's schema language has no native CHECK syntax). Verified live: prisma migrate deploy runs cleanly in both CI and the Docker backend entrypoint. **Day 1:** no swap needed — this is the real, migrated Postgres schema already backing every read/write; there is no separate mock persistence layer to retire.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: All columns/enums/indexes match ARCH §4 exactly; DB rejects quantity<=0 or price<=0 at the constraint level even if app validation were bypassed; prisma migrate deploy succeeds against a clean Postgres 16 instance.

SUMMARY: TradeRepository — Prisma-backed data access layer
USER_STORY: As the TradeService, I want a repository that encapsulates all Prisma calls for trades, so that business logic never talks to the ORM directly.
DESCRIPTION: Implements backend/src/repositories/tradeRepository.ts — list() (filter by symbol/trader/side/status, sort by any of 5 fields), findById, nextTradeId (sequential TRD-1000xx codes), create, update, cancel. All methods read and confirmed to hit the real Prisma client (backend/src/lib/prisma.ts), not an in-memory stub. **Day 1:** no swap needed — already the real Postgres-backed repository; there was never a mock data store to replace.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: list() applies all 4 optional filters and both sort directions; create/update/cancel persist and return the updated row; verified live via curl (create->list-filtered->amend->cancel->409-on-second-cancel).

SUMMARY: WebSocketBroadcaster — real-time transport
USER_STORY: As a connected client, I want to receive every trade mutation the instant it happens, so that my blotter view stays correct without polling or refreshing.
DESCRIPTION: Implements backend/src/realtime/webSocketBroadcaster.ts per ADR-003 — a raw ws WebSocketServer attached to the same http.Server instance Express listens on (one port), holding an in-memory Set<WebSocket> of open clients and calling .send() on all OPEN sockets on broadcast(). Confirmed wired into server.ts (new WebSocketBroadcaster(httpServer)) and called by TradeService after every successful mutation. **Day 1:** no swap needed — this is the real, single-instance WS broadcaster ADR-003 calls for; no message queue/pub-sub layer is in scope per that ADR's explicit consequences.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Broadcasts a {type, payload} envelope to every open socket on create/amend/cancel; closed sockets are pruned from the client Set; runs on the same port as the HTTP API (verified: server.ts calls httpServer.on('request', app) alongside the WS server).

SUMMARY: TradeService — business logic & status-transition rules
USER_STORY: As the API layer, I want a service that enforces trade status-transition rules and triggers real-time broadcasts, so that routes stay thin and rules are enforced in one place.
DESCRIPTION: Implements backend/src/services/tradeService.ts — create/amend/cancel each call the repository then broadcaster.broadcast(); amend/cancel both throw ConflictError (409) if the trade is already CANCELLED; getById throws NotFoundError (404) if missing. Verified by 5 passing unit tests (backend/test/tradeService.test.ts, repository mocked) covering create+broadcast, not-found, and both conflict paths, plus live curl confirming the 409 on double-cancel and on amending a cancelled trade. **Day 1:** no swap needed — this already enforces the real business rules against the real repository; there is no simplified Day-0 version of this logic to replace.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Amending or cancelling a CANCELLED trade returns 409 CONFLICT; every successful mutation calls broadcast() exactly once with the correct event type; tradeService.test.ts (5 tests) passes.

SUMMARY: Error handling — AppError hierarchy & centralized errorHandler middleware
USER_STORY: As an API consumer, I want a consistent JSON error envelope with a stable status-code mapping, so that I can handle failures predictably regardless of which endpoint or validator raised them.
DESCRIPTION: Implements backend/src/lib/errors.ts (AppError/ValidationError/NotFoundError/ConflictError) and backend/src/middleware/errorHandler.ts, which maps ZodError -> 400 VALIDATION_ERROR (with per-field messages), AppError subclasses -> their own status/code, and anything else -> logged 500 INTERNAL_ERROR. Matches the exact envelope shape and status-code table in ARCH §8. Curl-verified live: 400 on invalid payload, 404 on missing trade, 409 on double-cancel. **Day 1:** no swap needed — this is the real, permanent error-handling middleware wired into app.ts; there is no mock error layer.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Every thrown ZodError/AppError produces {error:{code,message,fields?}}; status codes match 400/404/409/500 exactly per ARCH §8; unhandled errors are logged via pino, not leaked to the client.

SUMMARY: Trade REST API routes + Express app wiring (CORS/helmet/body-limit/pino)
USER_STORY: As a frontend developer, I want the 5 documented REST endpoints exposed under /api, protected by CORS/security middleware, so that the blotter UI has a real API to call.
DESCRIPTION: Implements backend/src/routes/trades.ts (GET /trades, GET /trades/:id, POST /trades, PATCH /trades/:id, POST /trades/:id/cancel — matches ARCH §5 exactly) and backend/src/app.ts (helmet(), cors({origin: env.CORS_ORIGIN}), express.json({limit:'100kb'}), requestLogger via pino, mounted before errorHandler). Live curl walkthrough confirmed every endpoint's status code and payload shape; 8/8 route-level Supertest integration tests pass against a real Postgres instance. **Day 1:** no swap needed — every route already executes real Prisma-backed logic through TradeService; there is no mock-response version of these routes.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: All 5 endpoints return the documented status/shape; CORS restricts to CORS_ORIGIN; request body capped at 100kb; every request logged via pino (not console.log); backend/test/routes/trades.test.ts (8 tests) passes against real Postgres.

SUMMARY: Seed script — idempotent startup seed (~500 trades)
USER_STORY: As a reviewer running this app for the first time, I want realistic seeded data on first boot, so that the blotter isn't empty when I open it.
DESCRIPTION: Implements backend/src/seed.ts — checks prisma.trade.count() first and skips entirely if non-zero (idempotent across repeated docker compose up runs per ADR-002's consequences), otherwise generates 500 trades (within the brief's 100-1,000 range) with randomized symbol/side/quantity/price/trader/book/counterparty/timestamp/status (~10% pre-cancelled). Confirmed invoked automatically by backend/Dockerfile's CMD (prisma migrate deploy && pnpm run seed && pnpm start). **Day 1:** no swap needed — this is the real seed script that runs against the real database on every container boot, not a Day-0 placeholder.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Running seed twice in a row only inserts data once; generates between 100-1,000 trades; Docker boot runs it automatically before the server starts listening.

SUMMARY: apiClient.ts — typed fetch wrapper
USER_STORY: As a frontend developer, I want one typed client for all trade API calls, so that request/response shapes are enforced by the shared types rather than re-declared per call site.
DESCRIPTION: Implements frontend/src/lib/apiClient.ts — a request<T>() wrapper around fetch that reads VITE_API_BASE_URL, throws a typed ApiError (status/code/message/fields) on non-2xx, and exposes listTrades/getTrade/createTrade/amendTrade/cancelTrade, each typed against shared/. Confirmed it calls the real backend (no mock fixtures) — useTrades uses it directly. **Day 1:** no swap needed — already hitting the real REST API; there is no mock-fetch layer to retire.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Every method is typed against shared/trade.ts request/response shapes; non-2xx responses throw ApiError with the server's error code/fields intact.

SUMMARY: useTrades — TanStack Query hook (list + create/amend/cancel mutations)
USER_STORY: As the blotter UI, I want a single hook exposing trades plus create/amend/cancel mutations with automatic cache invalidation, so that every component reads one consistent source of trade data.
DESCRIPTION: Implements frontend/src/hooks/useTrades.ts — wraps apiClient.listTrades in a useQuery keyed by [...tradesQueryKey, filters], and createTrade/amendTrade/cancelTrade in useMutations that invalidate the trades query on success. Confirmed the filters state from TradeFilters flows into this hook's query key, and it's the sole data source TradeGrid/TradeBlotterPage render from. **Day 1:** no swap needed — already backed by the real API via apiClient; there is no mock-data version of this hook.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Changing any filter re-queries the real API with the new params; each mutation invalidates and refetches the trade list on success.

SUMMARY: useRealtimeTrades — WebSocket client with reconnect/backoff & cache reconciliation
USER_STORY: As a user with the blotter open, I want trades created/amended/cancelled by anyone else to appear in my view immediately, so that I never work from stale data.
DESCRIPTION: Implements frontend/src/hooks/useRealtimeTrades.ts — connects to VITE_WS_URL, reconnects with exponential backoff (1s to 30s cap) on unexpected close, and on each message reconciles the event directly into the exact TanStack Query cache key the blotter list reads (queryClient.setQueryData, matching filters) per ADR-004's explicit requirement — no forced refetch. Also fires the connection-lost/restored and per-event toasts required by ARCH §11. Proven correct by a dedicated mocked-WebSocket test suite (4/4 passing) covering all 3 event types plus filtered-cache removal on cancel. **Day 1:** no swap needed — already connects to and reconciles events from the real WebSocketBroadcaster; there is no simulated/mock event source.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: TRADE_CREATED/AMENDED/CANCELLED each update the cache correctly without a refetch; reconnect backoff caps at 30s; connection-lost and connection-restored toasts fire; useRealtimeTrades.test.tsx (4 tests) passes.

SUMMARY: Toast notification system (ToastProvider)
USER_STORY: As a user, I want visible feedback for real-time events, mutation results, and connection state changes, so that I know the app is responding without needing to guess.
DESCRIPTION: Implements frontend/src/components/Toast/ToastProvider.tsx, providing the useToast()/showToast() API consumed by useRealtimeTrades (event + connection toasts) and TradeBlotterPage (create/amend/cancel success/failure toasts) — covers all 4 toast cases ARCH §11 requires. **Day 1:** no swap needed — this is permanent UI infrastructure, not a mock or placeholder.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Exposes a context/hook consumable from anywhere in the tree; supports at minimum success/error/info/connection toast variants, matching the 4 cases in ARCH §11.

SUMMARY: TradeGrid — TanStack Table wrapper (sorting, side/status styling)
USER_STORY: As a user, I want to sort the blotter by any column and visually distinguish BUY/SELL and cancelled trades at a glance, so that I can scan the grid quickly.
DESCRIPTION: Implements frontend/src/components/TradeGrid.tsx using TanStack Table v9's useTable/tableFeatures/rowSortingFeature API — all 10 columns defined, client-side sorting (default sort: tradeTimestamp desc), BUY/SELL badge styling, CANCELLED rows dimmed (opacity-50), Amend/Cancel row actions hidden once cancelled. Note: sorting is applied client-side via TanStack Table's own row model rather than the API's sort=/order= query params described in ARCH §5 — functionally equivalent at the ~500-row scale this app targets, flagged here as a doc/implementation nuance rather than a gap. **Day 1:** no swap needed — renders real trade data from useTrades, not fixtures; component tests (TradeGrid.test.tsx) pass against real column/row rendering logic.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: All 10 documented columns render; clicking a sortable header toggles asc/desc; BUY/SELL have distinct styling; CANCELLED rows are visually dimmed and hide Amend/Cancel actions; TradeGrid.test.tsx passes.

SUMMARY: TradeFilters — symbol/trader/side/status filter controls
USER_STORY: As a user, I want to filter the blotter by symbol, trader, side, and status, so that I can narrow down to the trades I care about.
DESCRIPTION: Implements frontend/src/components/TradeFilters.tsx — controlled inputs/selects for all 4 filter fields, feeding a TradeListQuery object up to TradeBlotterPage's state, which flows into useTrades's query key. Confirmed not a no-op: each onChange immediately updates real query params. **Day 1:** no swap needed — already wired to the live query, not a static/demo filter bar.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Changing any filter control triggers a re-fetch with the corresponding query param; clearing a filter (empty string) omits that param entirely rather than sending an empty-string filter.

SUMMARY: CreateTradeModal / AmendTradeModal — React Hook Form + Zod forms
USER_STORY: As a user, I want to create a new trade or amend an existing one through a validated form, so that I can't submit invalid data and get the same validation rules the server enforces.
DESCRIPTION: Implements frontend/src/components/CreateTradeModal.tsx and AmendTradeModal.tsx (sharing TradeFormFields.tsx and Modal.tsx), both using useForm + zodResolver(createTradeSchema)/zodResolver(amendTradeSchema) from shared/. AmendTradeModal pre-fills all fields from the target trade. Component test (CreateTradeModal.test.tsx) passes. **Day 1:** no swap needed — submits directly to the real createTrade/amendTrade mutations, not a mock submit handler.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Client-side validation errors match the same rules as the backend's Zod schemas (single source of truth); successful submit calls the real mutation and closes the modal; CreateTradeModal.test.tsx passes.

SUMMARY: CancelTradeConfirm — inline confirm-and-cancel action
USER_STORY: As a user, I want a confirmation step before cancelling a trade, so that I don't cancel one by accident.
DESCRIPTION: Implements frontend/src/components/CancelTradeConfirm.tsx — an alertdialog overlay ("Keep Trade" / "Cancel Trade") triggered from a grid row's Cancel action, calling the real cancelTrade mutation on confirm. **Day 1:** no swap needed — confirms into the real cancel mutation, not a placeholder alert.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Dismissing leaves the trade untouched; confirming calls the real cancel mutation and closes the dialog regardless of success/failure (via finally).

SUMMARY: TradeBlotterPage — page composition (toolbar, grid, modals, toasts)
USER_STORY: As a user, I want a single page combining filters, actions, and the grid, so that the whole blotter workflow is in one place.
DESCRIPTION: Implements frontend/src/pages/TradeBlotterPage.tsx — composes TradeFilters, Refresh/New-Trade toolbar buttons, TradeGrid, and conditionally-rendered CreateTradeModal/AmendTradeModal/CancelTradeConfirm, wiring useTrades + useRealtimeTrades together and firing success/failure toasts around each mutation. Matches ARCH §11's functional layout exactly. **Day 1:** no swap needed — this is the real composed page rendering live data, not a static mockup.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Toolbar has filter fields, a working Refresh button, and a "New Trade" button; grid updates live via both manual refresh and WebSocket events; every mutation shows a success or failure toast.

SUMMARY: Docker Compose & Dockerfiles — local/containerized run
USER_STORY: As a reviewer, I want to run the entire stack with one command on any OS, so that I don't need to manually install or configure Postgres/Node.
DESCRIPTION: Implements docker-compose.yml (postgres:16-alpine + backend + frontend, each healthchecked, correct depends_on: condition: service_healthy ordering) and backend/Dockerfile/frontend/Dockerfile. Verified live: docker compose up -d --build boots all 3 services; backend's CMD runs prisma migrate deploy && pnpm run seed && pnpm start automatically on container start, matching the README's documented behavior exactly. **Day 1:** no swap needed — this is the real, working container setup used for the actual local-run path, not a scaffold placeholder.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: docker compose up succeeds from a clean checkout on Windows/Linux/Mac; backend healthcheck passes only once /health returns 200; frontend doesn't start until backend is healthy.

SUMMARY: CI pipeline — lint/typecheck/test/build against real Postgres
USER_STORY: As a maintainer, I want every push/PR to run lint, typecheck, the full test suite (against a real database), and a production build, so that regressions are caught before merge.
DESCRIPTION: Implements .github/workflows/ci.yml — a Postgres 16 service container, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, lint, typecheck, prisma migrate deploy, pnpm test, pnpm build, in that order. This is an extension beyond ARCH.md's Component Breakdown (§3 doesn't name a CI task explicitly) but is real, working infrastructure confirmed by reading the workflow file in full. Caveat: the workflow (and package.json's packageManager/pnpm-workspace.yaml) use **pnpm workspaces**, while ADR-001 literally documents "npm workspaces only" — a known, intentional deviation explained in knowledge/retros/day0-scaffold.md (a nexus tooling bug with package_manager:"pnpm" forced manual pnpm setup); ADR-001 itself was never updated to reflect this. Not a defect, but worth fixing at the doc level. **Day 1:** no swap needed — this is the real CI pipeline already running on every push, not a stub.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: CI fails on a lint/typecheck/test/build regression; integration tests run against a real Postgres service container, not a mock; ADR-001 gets corrected to say "pnpm workspaces" to match reality (tracked here since no other task owns doc upkeep).
